goal: The live page never shows a row twice. Twice on 2026-09-04 Martin's open `mc` drew the same session on two adjacent rows with two ages — `● items-sweep … 28 min` over `● items-sweep … 25 min`, then `sql-readiness ● plan 18 min` over `sql-readiness ● plan 11 min`, the same pid each time — and a restart of `mc` showed one. The data had one entry (the register, `current-*.json`, `mc --json` all said so); the screen had two.

The shape says what it is: the lower row is the fresh frame, the upper row is the previous frame's copy of the same line left standing one row above where the new one was printed. That happens when the page's arithmetic for *where its first row is on the screen* is off by one when a frame is drawn — `page-live.js` derives it (`above = footprint + tailRows`) and `page-frame.js` moves the cursor up by that number with relative `CSI A`. Any row that occupies two screen rows (a wrapped line, a glyph the terminal draws two cells wide) or any miscount of the rows under the page puts every later write one row off, and a grown frame — the one case that reprints from the page's first reachable row — leaves the old rows in place above the new ones.

So the page stops deriving where it is and asks the terminal. `CSI 6n` (Device Status Report — cursor position) answers `ESC [ row ; col R` on the input the live reader already owns in raw mode; read once after the page is printed and the prompt shown, that row is the anchor every frame is written against, and a resize or a scroll is a new question, not a recomputation.
contract: **The page's content and order do not change.** This is the drawing, not the sections; `page-render.js` is untouched. Martin, 2026-09-03: the overview of every project is the page's point, and RUNNER sits last so what moves is within reach.
**A pipe, a script and `--json` see no change at all** — `tests/mc/front-door.test.js` keeps asserting not one escape byte outside a terminal.
**Half-typed input survives every frame**, as `page-live.js` promises today; a fix that blanks the prompt line is not a fix.
**One step, one PR; everything lands through `mc merge`.**
out_of_scope: **Rows that have scrolled off the top.** `page-frame.js` says why they are history; the screen is what this project makes right.
**Terminals narrower than 60 columns** — still the plain reader, as `LIVE_MIN_COLUMNS` says.
**tmux** — the reproduction is a plain terminal (Martin: *"Ej TMUX"*); if the anchor also cures tmux, say so, do not chase it.

success_criteria.criterion: A frame drawn after the page has shifted one row — a wrapped key line, a resize — does not leave the previous row standing.
success_criteria.check: A test with a tail whose lines wrap at the fixture's width: the writes target the row the terminal reported, not `footprint + newlines`. Then Martin's terminal, left open across a step starting and ending, with no doubled row.

documents.label: The live page and the frame differ

steps.title: Ask the terminal where the page is, and draw every frame against that row
steps.done_when: `liveReader` (`src/mc/page-live.js`) reads the cursor row with `CSI 6n` after the page and the prompt are printed — on the `/dev/tty` stream it already holds in raw mode — and passes an absolute anchor to `frameWrites` (`src/mc/page-frame.js`), which moves with `CSI row;1H` rather than relative `CSI A`; a terminal that does not answer within 200 ms keeps the derived `above` and says `mc: drawing by count — the terminal did not say where the page is` in the note row once; resize re-asks; tests drive the answering, the silent and the wrapped-tail cases.
instruction: **Where the number comes from today.** `liveReader.ask` sets `tailRows = newlines(tail)` and `draw` computes `above = current.length + tailRows`; `frameWrites(previous, next, { above, rows })` in `page-frame.js` walks rows with `vertical(target - row)` and reprints a grown frame from `max(0, above - reach)` with `up(above - first)`. Every one of these is a count of *lines*, and the terminal counts *rows*: the two key lines under the page (`KEYS` in `commands/home.js`, 85 and 40 characters) wrap on a terminal narrower than that, and a wrapped line is two rows. The doubled rows Martin saw are one row of drift, exactly the kind of thing a miscount by one produces.

**Ask instead.** After `stdout.write(\`${tail}${prompt} \`)` in `ask`, write `CSI 6n` and read the reply `ESC [ <row> ; <col> R` from the raw input stream — `readLine`'s `onData` already sees every byte; give it a small pre-pass that swallows a DSR reply before it reaches the line editor, and resolve a promise with the row. The cursor then sits on the prompt row; the page's first row is that row minus the rows the page and the tail actually occupy *on screen*, which is what a second `6n` after `up(above)` would tell you exactly — or, simpler and enough: record the prompt row as the anchor and express every target as `promptRow - above + index`, so an error in `above` moves the whole frame together rather than leaving old rows behind. Read `page-frame.js`'s header before choosing; it says why `CSI L`/`CSI M` are not used and that constraint stays.

**Absolute moves.** `frameWrites` gets an optional `anchor` (the prompt's screen row); with it, a row's target is `CSI ${anchor - above + index};1H` and the return is `CSI ${anchor};${col}H`, and `rows` still bounds what is above the screen (row 1). Without it, the relative writes stay as they are — the plain fallback and the existing tests keep passing.

**When the terminal will not say.** 200 ms without a reply: keep `above`, draw as today, and put one line in the note row (`hold`'s row) saying so — never block the prompt on a terminal that ignores DSR. A resize (`stdout.on('resize')`) already marks the frame dirty; make it also re-ask.

**Tests** in `tests/mc/page-live.test.js`, beside the eight that exist: a fake input that answers `6n` with `\x1b[42;3R` and a frame whose writes carry `\x1b[<n>;1H` for the changed row; a fake that never answers and a frame drawn with relative moves plus the note; a tail whose key line wraps at the fixture's width, where the anchored frame lands on the right row and the derived one would not. `tests/mc/front-door.test.js` unchanged and green.
**Documentation.** `docs/technical/mc-ui.md` § *The live page*: one paragraph — the page asks the terminal where it is, why, and what it does when the terminal will not answer.
comments: The anchor alone would not have cured the doubled row, and that is worth knowing before anyone reads the diff and wonders why `tailRows` changed. A target is `anchor - above + index`, so a wrong `above` still moves every row — the anchor stops the error *accumulating* from row to row, it does not stop it. The `above` the page had was wrong for the reason the plan named: `tailRows` counted the newlines in the menu's block, and `KEYS[0]` in `commands/home.js` is 85 characters, which is two screen rows below 85 columns. So both halves landed — `screenRows(text, columns)` in `page-live.js` counts wrapped rows (exported, and unit-tested on its own), and `frameWrites` takes the anchor. This is what the plan's instruction called "the rows the page and the tail actually occupy on screen"; it is not extra scope, it is the half without which the wrapped-tail test could not pass.

The page's own rows are still counted one row per line, deliberately. `page-render.js` clips every row to `columnsFor(columns)`, so a page row is not supposed to wrap — and if one ever did, `frameWrites`'s index-to-row map would be wrong per row, which a single `above` cannot express. If a double-width glyph ever does push a page row over the edge, the fix is in the index map, not in `above`. Nothing in this step touched `page-render.js`.

Two things the runner's gate cannot see. First, criterion 2's second half — Martin's own terminal, left open across a step starting and ending, with no doubled row — has not been run and cannot be from here, which is why that criterion is still `met: false`; `scripts/mc-live-page-check.mjs` is the pty harness that would come closest and is not part of `npm test` (five and a half minutes). Second, criterion 3 is written but its check says "on main", so it stays `false` until this lands. Also unmeasured: whether the anchor cures tmux, which the plan put out of scope — no claim is made either way.

One behavioural change that is easy to miss in review: after a growth or resize reprint the loop now re-asks `CSI 6n`, so a reprint frame ends with `\x1b[6n` rather than with the half-typed answer. Two existing tests asserted `endsWith` on that write and now assert `includes` plus an explicit `endsWith(DSR)`. Six other existing tests were given an `advance(1_000)` before their mark so the 200 ms by-count note falls outside the slice they measure — the note is real behaviour on a silent fake terminal, not test noise.
